import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source CSV files
source_files = {
    "whites": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_23/training_0.csv",
    "mixed": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_23/training_1.csv",
    "aian": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_23/training_2.csv",
    "black": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_23/training_3.csv",
    "other": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_23/training_4.csv",
    "hispanic": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_23/training_5.csv",
}

# Load each source table with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df_whites = pd.read_csv(source_files["whites"], index_col=0)
df_mixed = pd.read_csv(source_files["mixed"], index_col=0)
df_aian = pd.read_csv(source_files["aian"], index_col=0)
df_black = pd.read_csv(source_files["black"], index_col=0)
df_other = pd.read_csv(source_files["other"], index_col=0)
df_hispanic = pd.read_csv(source_files["hispanic"], index_col=0)

# The key columns to join on are: CountyID, CountyName, Year, ID
# All source tables share these columns except the population column differs.

# To avoid ambiguity and to match the target schema, we will join all tables on these keys:
join_keys = ["CountyID", "CountyName", "Year", "ID"]

# Start joining step by step, renaming columns to match target schema after join

# Join whites and other (both have 'CountyID', 'CountyName', 'Year', 'ID' plus population column)
df_join_0 = pd.merge(
    df_whites,
    df_other,
    on=join_keys,
    how="outer",
    suffixes=("_x", "_y"),
)

# Join the result with mixed
df_join_1 = pd.merge(
    df_join_0,
    df_mixed,
    on=join_keys,
    how="outer",
    suffixes=("", "_mixed"),
)

# Join with hispanic
df_join_2 = pd.merge(
    df_join_1,
    df_hispanic,
    on=join_keys,
    how="outer",
    suffixes=("", "_hispanic"),
)

# Join with black
df_join_3 = pd.merge(
    df_join_2,
    df_black,
    on=join_keys,
    how="outer",
    suffixes=("", "_black"),
)

# Join with aian
df_join_4 = pd.merge(
    df_join_3,
    df_aian,
    on=join_keys,
    how="outer",
    suffixes=("", "_aian"),
)

# Now we have all population columns in one dataframe, but columns from different sources have suffixes or original names.
# We need to rename and duplicate columns to match the target schema exactly.

# Target schema columns:
# ['CountyID_x', 'CountyName_x', 'whites_population', 'Year_x', 'ID',
#  'CountyID_y', 'CountyName_y', 'other_population', 'Year_y',
#  'CountyID_x_9', 'CountyName_x_10', 'mixed_population', 'Year_x_12',
#  'CountyID_y_13', 'CountyName_y_14', 'hispanic_population', 'Year_y_16',
#  'CountyID_x_17', 'CountyName_x_18', 'black_population', 'Year_x_20',
#  'CountyID_y_21', 'CountyName_y_22', 'aian_population', 'Year_y_24']

# The pattern is that for each population type, the key columns are repeated with suffixes.
# We will create these repeated columns by duplicating the key columns accordingly.

# Prepare a new DataFrame with all required columns

df_result = pd.DataFrame()

# whites_population block
df_result["CountyID_x"] = df_join_4["CountyID"]
df_result["CountyName_x"] = df_join_4["CountyName"]
df_result["whites_population"] = df_join_4["whites_population"]
df_result["Year_x"] = df_join_4["Year"]
df_result["ID"] = df_join_4["ID"]

# other_population block (suffix _y)
df_result["CountyID_y"] = df_join_4["CountyID"]
df_result["CountyName_y"] = df_join_4["CountyName"]
df_result["other_population"] = df_join_4["other_population"]
df_result["Year_y"] = df_join_4["Year"]

# mixed_population block (suffix _x_9 and _x_10 for CountyID and CountyName, Year_x_12 for Year)
df_result["CountyID_x_9"] = df_join_4["CountyID"]
df_result["CountyName_x_10"] = df_join_4["CountyName"]
df_result["mixed_population"] = df_join_4["mixed_population"]
df_result["Year_x_12"] = df_join_4["Year"]

# hispanic_population block (suffix _y_13 and _y_14 for CountyID and CountyName, Year_y_16 for Year)
df_result["CountyID_y_13"] = df_join_4["CountyID"]
df_result["CountyName_y_14"] = df_join_4["CountyName"]
df_result["hispanic_population"] = df_join_4["hispanic_population"]
df_result["Year_y_16"] = df_join_4["Year"]

# black_population block (suffix _x_17 and _x_18 for CountyID and CountyName, Year_x_20 for Year)
df_result["CountyID_x_17"] = df_join_4["CountyID"]
df_result["CountyName_x_18"] = df_join_4["CountyName"]
df_result["black_population"] = df_join_4["black_population"]
df_result["Year_x_20"] = df_join_4["Year"]

# aian_population block (suffix _y_21 and _y_22 for CountyID and CountyName, Year_y_24 for Year)
df_result["CountyID_y_21"] = df_join_4["CountyID"]
df_result["CountyName_y_22"] = df_join_4["CountyName"]
df_result["aian_population"] = df_join_4["aian_population"]
df_result["Year_y_24"] = df_join_4["Year"]

# Fill NaN population values with 0 and convert to integer (population counts)
pop_columns = [
    "whites_population",
    "other_population",
    "mixed_population",
    "hispanic_population",
    "black_population",
    "aian_population",
]

for col in pop_columns:
    df_result[col] = df_result[col].fillna(0).astype(int)

# For the key columns, fill missing values if any (should not happen if join keys are consistent)
key_columns = [
    "CountyID_x", "CountyName_x", "Year_x", "ID",
    "CountyID_y", "CountyName_y", "Year_y",
    "CountyID_x_9", "CountyName_x_10", "Year_x_12",
    "CountyID_y_13", "CountyName_y_14", "Year_y_16",
    "CountyID_x_17", "CountyName_x_18", "Year_x_20",
    "CountyID_y_21", "CountyName_y_22", "Year_y_24",
]

# For integer ID columns, fillna with 0 and convert to int
id_columns = [
    "CountyID_x", "Year_x",
    "CountyID_y", "Year_y",
    "CountyID_x_9", "Year_x_12",
    "CountyID_y_13", "Year_y_16",
    "CountyID_x_17", "Year_x_20",
    "CountyID_y_21", "Year_y_24",
    "ID",
]

for col in id_columns:
    df_result[col] = df_result[col].fillna(0).astype(int)

# For CountyName columns, fillna with empty string
name_columns = [
    "CountyName_x", "CountyName_y",
    "CountyName_x_10", "CountyName_y_14",
    "CountyName_x_18", "CountyName_y_22",
]

for col in name_columns:
    df_result[col] = df_result[col].fillna("")

# Reorder columns exactly as target schema
target_columns = [
    'CountyID_x', 'CountyName_x', 'whites_population', 'Year_x', 'ID',
    'CountyID_y', 'CountyName_y', 'other_population', 'Year_y',
    'CountyID_x_9', 'CountyName_x_10', 'mixed_population', 'Year_x_12',
    'CountyID_y_13', 'CountyName_y_14', 'hispanic_population', 'Year_y_16',
    'CountyID_x_17', 'CountyName_x_18', 'black_population', 'Year_x_20',
    'CountyID_y_21', 'CountyName_y_22', 'aian_population', 'Year_y_24'
]

df_result = df_result[target_columns]

# Write the result to the specified CSV file path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_23/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_result.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
